The largest country in the world is Russia.

To understand the concept of relativity described in your text, imagine time as a river. In our everyday lives, we assume this river flows at a constant speed for everyone, everywhere. However, Einstein’s theory of relativity suggests that the "flow" of this river can actually speed up or slow down depending on how fast you are moving or how strong the gravity is around you.

Think of the train moving near the speed of light as a boat trying to race against the current. For the person on the boat (you), the water feels normal, and your watch ticks at its usual pace. But for someone standing on the shore (the outside observer), it looks like the boat is moving so incredibly fast that the water around it seems to freeze or move in slow motion. In this analogy, the "slow motion" water represents time ticking slower for the traveler compared to the person on the shore. This isn't an illusion; it is a fundamental property of the universe where time and space are interconnected and flexible.
